description: Service-model allocation shares by control layer, on-premises sections and responsibility functions, COBIT pillars, platform lifecycle stages and failure scenarios used by the Shared Responsibility Explorer.

service_models.definition: The organisation operates the full technology stack in facilities it controls.
The provider operates physical infrastructure and virtualisation; the customer manages operating systems, workloads, data and most security configuration.
The provider operates the infrastructure and application platform; the customer manages applications, identities, data and configuration.
The provider operates the application and supporting stack; the customer manages use, identities, data, configuration and monitoring integration.
The provider operates the event-driven runtime and infrastructure; the customer manages function code, identities, data, triggers and configuration.
Backend as a Service provides managed databases, user authentication, push notifications and other pre-made backend capabilities so developers can focus on the client-side application.
Security as a Service integrates capabilities such as anti-malware, authentication and intrusion detection into the customer’s cloud environment.
Desktop as a Service delivers provider-hosted virtual desktop infrastructure so users can stream a managed desktop environment to supported devices.
Database as a Service provides a managed database without requiring the customer to provision physical hardware or install and operate database software.
Identity as a Service outsources digital gatekeeping—including authentication, password infrastructure and multi-factor authentication—to an identity provider such as Microsoft Entra ID.
Containers as a Service provides managed servers and container orchestration, such as Kubernetes; the customer manages containers, images, configuration and application code.

failure_scenarios.title: Primary server room flood
failure_scenarios.label: Scenario 1 · Primary server room flood
failure_scenarios.summary: A burst water pipe destroys the primary VMware cluster, SAN and on-site backup NAS. The disaster-recovery team must activate a branch recovery site and restore critical on-premises services from the latest usable off-site copy.
failure_scenarios.objective: Restore Tier 1 systems within 4 hours, Tier 2 systems within 8 hours, and limit data loss to 24 hours.

failure_scenarios.title: Cloud identity outage
failure_scenarios.label: Scenario 2 · Cloud identity outage
failure_scenarios.summary: The cloud identity provider stops authenticating users, locking staff and administrators out of cloud services, VPN access and federated on-premises applications while the underlying hardware remains available.
failure_scenarios.objective: Regain identity-tenant administration within 30 minutes, restore critical remote access within 2 hours, and make ERP and email usable within 4 hours.

failure_scenarios.title: Malware outbreak
failure_scenarios.label: Scenario 3 · Malware outbreak
failure_scenarios.summary: Ransomware spreads from a phished endpoint into the server network, encrypting file shares, virtual machines and the backup NAS. Containment, evidence preservation and clean identity recovery must precede restoration.
failure_scenarios.objective: Contain spread within 1 hour, rebuild or verify clean identity within 24 hours, restore Tier 1 systems within 48 hours, and complete hardened recovery within 2 weeks.

failure_scenarios.title: On-premises gateway failure
failure_scenarios.label: Scenario 4 · On-premises gateway failure
failure_scenarios.summary: The edge firewall fails after a firmware update, cutting the office off from internet, cloud, remote users and branch connectivity while internal servers remain operational and no data restore is required.
failure_scenarios.objective: Provide temporary internet access for critical staff within 1 hour, restore VPN and site-to-site tunnels within 4 hours, and complete permanent replacement within one business day.
phases: Fail over or replace the gateway
